doc.title: Packages
doc.paragraph: You may find yourself using Adaptive Framework Core in order to build something of your own. There's nothing that prevents you from setting up your own project to use Adaptive Framework, but you may find that the afwdev provides some convenient helper commands to get you started and to maintain your project. A project that uses afwdev to build and maintain is called a Package.

Packages are Git repositories that hold one or more commands, extensions, configurations, objects or layouts using Adaptive Framework and maintained using the afwdev tool. The following illustrates the file system layout of a typical package:
doc.code: <AFW package root directory> |-- doc/ # Generated docs |-- generated/ # Produced by generate subcommand | |-- *.cmake # Generated cmake files | |-- <PACKAGE_ID>_git_info.sh # Used to produce <PACKAGE_ID>_git_info.h | |-- <PACKAGE_ID>_git_info.h # Header file containing git information | |-- schemas/ # JSON Schemas for the package's objects |-- src/ # Commonly src/ contains source directories | |-- <SRCDIR>/ # One or more command, extension, or server | |-- generate/ # Processed by generate subcommand | |-- generated/ # Produced by generate subcommand | | |-- c source # Generated *.h and .c files | | |-- *.cmake # Generated cmake files | | |-- ... # Other generated files and directories | |-- c source # <SRCDIR>_*.h and .c files | |-- CMakeLists.txt # CMakeLists.txt for <SRCDIR> | |-- ... # Other source files and directories |-- .editorconfig # Source editor coding style |-- .gitattributes # Command git attributes for pathnames |-- .gitignore # Command git files to ignore |-- afw-package.json # AFW package file managed by the afwdev |-- CMakeLists.txt # Root CMakeLists.txt for afw package |-- COPYING # Licensing information. |-- Doxyfile # Doxygen configuration file |-- LICENSE # The license. |-- afwdev # Runs afwdev from this package's source |-- package.json # Used to build a JavaScript package |-- README.md # Repository README.md |-- miscellaneous directories # Other directories |-- miscellaneous files # Other files

section.title: Creating a New Package
section.paragraph: New Package are created using the afwdev make-afw-package subcommand.

section.title: Building Against an Installed Adaptive Framework
section.paragraph: A package outside of the afw repository builds against the Adaptive Framework that is installed, usually under /usr/local. Its CMake files find it with find_package(afw). Each install leaves a versioned directory, such as lib/cmake/afw-0.12.2, next to the ones before it, and the root CMakeLists.txt that make-afw-package writes picks the newest one for you. Your C sources only need #include "afw.h". That header brings in the public API, including the AFW_DECLARE and AFW_DEFINE macros from afw_common.h. Headers named *_internal.h belong to the library that owns them and are not installed.

Adaptive Framework does not use APR. Neither find_package(afw) nor afw.pc asks for it, and no Adaptive Framework function takes or returns an APR pool. If your own code still uses APR for something else, link it yourself.

When you install a new Adaptive Framework, rebuild and reinstall your package against it. Using extensions or commands built against one install with the libafw of another is not supported. The version check only goes so far: before 1.0, an extension loads when its MAJOR and MINOR versions match the library's, even if the C API changed in between. If you are bringing a package up to date from an older Adaptive Framework, the C programmers and Updating another repository sections of whats-new.md list what changed.

section.title: Generated JSON Schemas
section.paragraph: Every time you generate, afwdev also writes a JSON Schema for each object type into generated/schemas/. Like everything else under generated/, these files are not edited by hand: change the object type under generate/objects/ and generate again.
